title: Technical deep dive - OpenTelemetry & token metrics (KV cache, batching)
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Lumina Labs platform and ML leads through OpenTelemetry integration options for token-level metrics, tracing span design for inference runtime, and how to surface KV-cache and batching telemetry in dashboards. Customer cares about private/VPC deployments, encryption/KMS, and end-to-end traces for debugging latency spikes. Agreed next steps: share integration guide, run a short trace-enabled pilot, and provide a sample Grafana dashboard + alert rules.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-29 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Elena (Redwood Solutions), Jasper (Lumina CTO), Amaya (Lead ML), Mark (Platform), Rita (Security)

00:00:04 Maya Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we have about an hour, quick intros?
00:00:12 Jasper Lee: Jasper here, CTO at Lumina, we run a mix of real time and batch inference, interested in observability for our private deployment.
00:00:20 Amaya Rodriguez: hi, i'm Amaya, i own ML infra and model performance, we're seeing occasional tail latency, want to instrument token-level metrics to correlate with KV cache hits.
00:00:32 Mark Chen: Mark, platform, mainly VPC and networking questions.
00:00:36 Rita O'Neill: Rita from security, SOC2/SSO/KMS questions later.
00:00:41 Maya Patel: thanks - i'll hand to Samir to kick off with how we do tracing and token metrics on Redwood.

00:00:52 Samir Khatri: cool, so big picture — Redwood exposes an OpenTelemetry-compatible hook. you can either push spans from the runtime via a local otel-collector, or have the runtime export to our managed ingest over TLS. we instrument per-request spans: inbound request -> routing -> model serve -> kv-cache lookup -> token generation loop. the token loop emits token-level metrics optionally.
00:01:15 Amaya Rodriguez: sorry did you say token-level metrics are emitted per token? that could be a lot of telemetry.
00:01:22 Samir Khatri: yeah good call—it's configurable. we sample at a rate, and we also emit aggregated histograms per request: tokens per second, p95 token latency, cache hit ratio. token-level (per-token) is useful for debugging KV-cache cold-starts or degredation in quantized kernels, but for prod we recommend 1% sampling + per-route aggregated metrics.
00:01:50 Jasper Lee: ok, and how does KV cache visibility look? we need to see hit rates, eviction rates, and maybe top keys missing.
00:01:58 Samir Khatri: we emit KV cache spans and metrics: kv.hit, kv.miss, kv.evictions, and you can correlate span ids to request ids. caveat: for privacy we don't log raw keys by default, but can emit hashed keys or sampled keys if you enable debug mode.
00:02:18 Amaya Rodriguez: hashed keys is fine. we want to tie cache misses to token-level latency spikes.

00:02:34 Elena Gomez: quick note on quantization observability: when you run a quantized model we tag spans with quant.profile and kernel variant, so you can filter traces to see if a particular quant path has higher token latency. sometimes small model substitutions (4-bit vs 8-bit) change perf in tail cases.
00:02:50 Mark Chen: on the VPC side, how do we get traces out? we can't allow outbound 443 to the public.
00:02:59 Samir Khatri: for Private/VPC you run an otel-collector inside your VPC and forward to your own backend or to our private ingress via peered link. we support mutual TLS + customer certs. Elena can share collector config.
00:03:12 Rita O'Neill: do you have SOC2 docs that cover audit logging for traces and PII handling?
00:03:18 Maya Patel: yes we'll include SOC2 and data handling docs in the follow-up; traces are treated as telemetry and we redact PII by default, you can add sensitive masking rules.

00:03:33 [00:03:33] Topic change: Instrumentation patterns and OTEL schema
00:03:36 Samir Khatri: we recommend these span names and attributes: span.model.inference, span.kv.lookup, attr.model.version, attr.seq_len, attr.route, attr.customer_id (hashed). for token-level metrics we use metrics: inference.tokens_emitted, inference.token_latency_ms and label by model, route, quant_profile.
00:04:05 Amaya Rodriguez: can we see an example Grafana dashboard?
00:04:08 Maya Patel: yep we'll send a sample that shows p50/p95/p99 token latency, kv hit ratio, batch size distribution, caller-side vs server-side latency.

00:04:22 Jasper Lee: about batching — we use dynamic batching at the runtime; if we batch too much we see higher p99. can we get per-batch metrics?
00:04:30 Samir Khatri: yes, per-batch metrics: batch.size, batch.latency, batch.queue_time. batching policy tags are part of spans so you can group traces by batch window size. also we export continuous-batching diagnostics—when the kernel waits for the batch window it emits a wait span.
00:04:49 Amaya Rodriguez: is there a recommended approach to correlate client-side request timeouts with server token emission?
00:04:56 Samir Khatri: tie request id across client and server spans — we support propagating a traceparent header. then you can see if the server emitted tokens after client timeout. we also emit a stream.closed event when streaming stops mid-inference.

00:05:12 [00:05:12] Interruption / crosstalk
00:05:15 Mark Chen: sorry, another network question — for peered link we get forced NAT sometimes, does that break mTLS?
00:05:22 Samir Khatri: usually no, but you need end-to-end mTLS and keep certificate CNs consistent. we'll check the exact peering setup.

00:05:30 [00:05:30] 10-minute deep dive: token-level sampling and storage costs
00:05:32 Samir Khatri: we also discussed costs: token-level telemetry increases storage and egress costs. pragmatic approach: sample 1% token-level with aggregation for the rest; store raw token samples for 7 days and aggregated for 90 days. this keeps costs bounded while enabling debugging.
00:05:54 Amaya Rodriguez: what about regulatory retention? we might need to keep certain audit trails longer for compliance.
00:06:01 Rita O'Neill: yes retention policy is important.
00:06:05 Maya Patel: we can work on retention SLAs in the Private contract.

00:06:18 [00:06:18] 20-minute marker, latency repro discussion
00:06:20 Jasper Lee: our tail spikes usually occur with long sequences (~2k tokens) and occasionally when quantized kernels fall back to a slower path. can we detect kernel fallback events?
00:06:29 Samir Khatri: we tag spans when a fallback happens: kernel.variant_changed, and emit a warning metric. you'll be able to drill into traces where fallback occurred.
00:06:40 Amaya Rodriguez: can we set alerts on kernel fallback rate?
00:06:43 Samir Khatri: yes, alert on kernel.fallback.count / minute or percent of requests.

00:06:52 [00:06:52] 30-minute marker, demo of sample trace (Samir shares screen)
00:06:55 Samir Khatri: showing a trace, here's a request with a kv.miss at 0.2s then token emission starts, you can see batch.wait for 50ms then kernel compute for 40ms per token. trace ids tie to request ids.
00:07:14 Amaya Rodriguez: looks useful—that kv.miss lined up exactly with the p99 on our logs.
00:07:20 Jasper Lee: question on sensitive data — are any request payloads or tokens ever stored raw in traces?
00:07:27 Samir Khatri: not by default. we hash or redact input text in telemetry. debug mode can capture examples but needs opt-in and access controls.

00:07:42 [00:07:42] Security mini-Q&A
00:07:44 Rita O'Neill: what encryption at rest is used for telemetry if we ship to Redwood ingest for hosted?
00:07:50 Maya Patel: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest, KMS-managed keys. for private we let you control the KMS.
00:07:58 Rita O'Neill: ok we'll need the encryption and key rotation docs.

00:08:10 [00:08:10] 40-minute marker, integration mechanics and sample configs
00:08:12 Samir Khatri: architecture patterns: 1) collector in VPC -> your observability backend, 2) collector in VPC -> private peered ingest -> Redwood observability (for Redwood-managed dashboards), 3) sidecar per inference node emitting spans locally. sample otel-collector configs and Jaeger/OTLP examples are in the guide.
00:08:35 Mark Chen: if we run sidecar we worry about CPU overhead on inference nodes. what's the overhead?
00:08:41 Samir Khatri: overhead is low if you batch metrics and send via UDP/OTLP; token-level emission per-token is the main cost. sidecars are recommended for low-latency networks; collector pattern reduces CPU on the node.

00:08:58 [00:08:58] 50-minute marker, rollout and dashboards
00:09:00 Elena Gomez: dashboards we provide: per-route latency, token histograms, kv.hit_ratio, batch size heatmap, quant_profile comparison. alerting recipes: p99 token latency increase >20% for 15 minutes, kv.miss_rate increase >5% in 5 minutes, kernel.fallback.rate >2% of requests.
00:09:19 Amaya Rodriguez: can we get a Grafana JSON so we can import?
00:09:23 Maya Patel: yes, we'll include Grafana and Prometheus queries.

00:09:30 [Final 5 minutes, recap and next steps]
00:09:33 Maya Patel: recap — we'll send the integration guide, sample dashboard, collector configs, and SOC2/encryption docs. Samir will provide collector example for Private/VPC. Lumina to run a short pilot with sampled token telemetry and share traces. action items on the doc.
00:09:50 Jasper Lee: thanks everyone, schedule follow-up 2 weeks after pilot start.
00:09:55 Amaya Rodriguez: thanks, this was helpful.
00:10:00 Maya Patel: great, we'll follow up by friday. bye all.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-generated captions had occasional typos ("Opentelemetery"), speaker labels sometimes conflated. timestamps approximate.
